knowledge_point.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y &=12 \\ -x-2y &=-6 \\ -x-2y &=-6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 4 & 12 \\ -1 & -2 & -6 \\ -1 & -2 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 4 & 12 \\ -1 & -2 & -6 \\ -1 & -2 & -6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 6 \\ -1 & -2 & -6 \\ -1 & -2 & -6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & -6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$, and we have one free variable, $y$. That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-2y+6 \\ y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-2y+6 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z &=-5 \\ -2x-y-2z &=6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -5 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -5 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-1 \\ y+2z &=-4.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-1 \\ y &=-2z-4 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2z-4 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+3z &=-7 \\ -x-y-z &=4.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & -7 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & -7 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-z &=-1 \\ y+2z &=-3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=z-1 \\ y &=-2z-3 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}z-1 \\ -2z-3 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+15z &=-3 \\ -2x+5y-35z &=6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 15 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -35 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 15 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -35 & 6\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 15 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+5z &=-3 \\ y-5z &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-5z-3 \\ y &=5z \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-5z-3 \\ 5z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z &=-8 \\ 2x-2y+3z &=-19.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -8 \\ 2 & -2 & 3 & -19\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -8 \\ 2 & -2 & 3 & -19\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y &=-5 \\ z &=-3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $y$. That means we need to find $x$ and $z$ in terms of $y$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=y-5 \\ y &=y \\ z &=-3,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}y-5 \\ y \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
